proposed:
Let \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\) be the structural H\"older-propensity subclass in \(\texttt{def:holder-propensity-triangular-law-class}\).  On every training complement use the clipped finite-net least-squares learner specified in \(\texttt{def:propensity-rate-regimes}\).  Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\),
\[
\max_{1\le k\le K}\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}
=O_{P_n}\!\left(n^{-t_\pi/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\right).
\]
reason: The current uniform quantifier ranges over laws that need not have a H"older propensity.  The replacement restricts it to the structural H"older-propensity subclass, exactly the laws for which the finite-net approximation step is valid.

current:
Under \(ass:holder-propensity\), the finite-net propensity learner and \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\) satisfy the hypotheses of \(thm:regular-efficient-inference\) whenever
\[
s>\frac D2,\qquad \frac{t_\pi}{2t_\pi+d_X}+\frac{s}{2s+D}>\frac12.
\]
The second inequality is equivalent to \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\). If the propensity is known, take \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\pi_n\) and \(r_{\pi,n}=0\), so only \(s>D/2\) remains. If a correctly specified fixed-dimensional propensity learner has the uniform rate \(r_{\pi,n}=n^{-1/2}\), its product condition is automatic and again only \(s>D/2\) remains.
proposed:
Over \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\), use the finite-net propensity learner and \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\).  These learners satisfy the nuisance-rate hypotheses of \(\texttt{thm:regular-efficient-inference}\) whenever
\[
s>\frac D2,\qquad \frac{t_\pi}{2t_\pi+d_X}+\frac{s}{2s+D}>\frac12.
\]
The second inequality is equivalent to \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\).  For any predetermined variance-separated collection on which the propensity is known, take \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\pi_n\) and \(r_{\pi,n}=0\), so only \(s>D/2\) remains.  For any such collection on which a correctly specified fixed-dimensional propensity learner has the uniform rate \(r_{\pi,n}=n^{-1/2}\), the product condition is automatic and again only \(s>D/2\) remains.
reason: The primitive rate verification must be quantified over the H"older-propensity subclass, while the known- and parametric-propensity corollaries require their own explicit uniform premises.

Assume the generic uniform propensity learner-rate condition in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\). Under the conclusions of \(lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates\), uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\),
\[\max_k\left|E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n})\right|=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}),\]
and
\[\max_k\left\|\widehat S_{-k,n}-(\theta_n+\psi_n)\right\|_{L^2(P_n)}=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}).\]
proposed:
Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) be predetermined, and assume that the generic propensity learner-rate condition in \(\texttt{def:propensity-rate-regimes}\) holds uniformly over \(\mathscr C\).  Under the conclusions of \(\texttt{lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates}\), uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr C\),
\[
\max_k\left|E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n})\right|=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}),
\]
and
\[
\max_k\left\|\widehat S_{-k,n}-(\theta_n+\psi_n)\right\|_{L^2(P_n)}=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}).

reason: A predetermined propensity learner may satisfy its uniform rate only on a predetermined collection.  Restricting the quantifier to that collection avoids inserting learner performance into the parent model class.

Suppose \(O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are i.i.d., \(E[\psi_n]=0\), \(|\psi_n|\le M\), \(E[\psi_n^2]=\sigma_n^2\ge\sigma_\star^2\),
\[\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),\qquad \widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=o_{P_n}(1),\]uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\). Then the studentized statistic converges uniformly in Kolmogorov distance to \(N(0,1)\), \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly, the denominator is positive with probability tending uniformly to one, and the associated two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).
proposed:
Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) be predetermined.  Suppose, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr C\), that \(O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are i.i.d., \(E_{P_n}[\psi_n]=0\), \(|\psi_n|\le M\), and
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),\qquad
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=o_{P_n}(1).
\]
Then the studentized statistic converges to \(N(0,1)\) uniformly over \(\mathscr C\) in Kolmogorov distance, \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the associated two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).
reason: Uniform studentization requires variance separation for every sequence under the supremum.  The replacement restricts the result to a predetermined collection inside the variance-separated class.

=-\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)\le0,
\]
and its absolute value has order \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\).

Under the hypotheses of \(lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates\) and \(lem:assignment-score-rates\), the exact conditional fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)

\]

\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})
+O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}r_{S,n}),
\]
and \(\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2})\).

The exact conditional fold bias is

Theorem 2 (conditional observational DML for the sharp COT endpoint). Fix the predetermined triangular law class \(\mathscr P\) in \(def:predetermined-triangular-law-class\). Use the normalized coupled learners in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the density route in \(def:foldwise-rate-route\), and a predetermined propensity learner satisfying the generic uniform rate condition in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\) for a deterministic \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). Suppose
\[
r_{q,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}+r_{q,n}=o(1).
\]
Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\), the exact fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)
+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)
\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}),
\]
where \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}\ge0\). Its two terms have orders \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) and \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\). Moreover,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+R_n,
\quad
R_n=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}))=o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2})=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}
\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0.
\]
Also \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). Its leading variance is the efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2\).
proposed:
Theorem 2 (conditional observational DML for the sharp COT endpoint).  Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) be any predetermined collection.  Use the predetermined normalized coupled learners in \(\texttt{def:coupled-fold-learners}\) and suppose their displayed uniform conditional-density rate premise holds over \(\mathscr C\).  Use a predetermined propensity learner satisfying the generic uniform \(L^2(P_{X,n})\) rate premise in \(\texttt{def:propensity-rate-regimes}\) over \(\mathscr C\), for deterministic \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\).  Suppose
\[
r_{q,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}+r_{q,n}=o(1).
\]
Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr C\), the exact fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)
+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)
\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}),
\]
where \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}\ge0\), and its two terms have orders \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) and \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\).  Moreover,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+R_n,
\quad
R_n=O_{P_n}\!\left(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n})\right)=o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2})=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}
\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0.
\]
Also \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly over \(\mathscr C\), \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and
\[
\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}P_n\!\left(\theta_n\in\left[\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n\right]\right)\to1-\alpha.
\]
The influence function is the observed-data canonical gradient \(\psi_n\), so the leading variance \(\sigma_n^2\) attains the semiparametric efficiency bound.
reason: The current theorem quantifies over the same parent class that must admit equality.  The replacement restricts only the inference theorem to a predetermined collection inside the variance-separated class and states both nuisance-rate requirements as estimator-side premises over that collection.
